setup: One stopped native 300 × 19 × 8 hull and one copied fixed-cabin test hull on a new dedicated server. Two survival non-operator player accounts are simulated on the server. The driver called production CabinApproach.begin twice during the same tick. The normal survey interface and its advance terrain loading were outside this test.
limits: First surface-berth planning took 330.3 ms and the second cold berth took 1403.4 ms. Assembly spent 1842.4 ms combined on tick 51. Physics transfer entry took 1008.7 and 2043.9 ms on separate ticks. Ordinary graphical confirmations are scheduled by LandingControl and need a separate concurrent client test.

normalSurvey.setup: Two simulated non-operator survival captains on a loopback-only dedicated Forge server with zero clients. The original wide ship and its copy begin prepositioned near the Moon. Both use normal survey polling and confirm on the same server tick.

fixtureControl.observed: Sending SURVEY once per seat left no live survey by the end of this trial. The retest models the open landing screen polling both surveys while they advance.

normalSurvey.limits: Native assembly still spent 859 and 975 milliseconds on separate ticks. Graphical clients, player discoverability and production server performance were outside this trial.

sharedStoragePreloading.scenario: Two independent loopback dedicated server runs from the same stopped 300×19×8 reference ship. Two simulated survival pilots, normal survey, confirmation and physical passage. No game clients.
sharedStoragePreloading.scope: Both warmers have claimed physical chunk tickets for 54 overlapping ticks. All source and target storage chunks are ready before each portal and the portals use separate ticks. The last dispatch is 27–29 ticks sooner. The second native portal and passage wall time increase in both runs, so these trials do not establish a lower worst-case tick.

hostedFirstGuiAttempt.observed: Both players entered the original Moon and both died during delivery. The first fixture equipped the original pressure suit but not the sealed GalaxySpace suit. The server notice was generic. The rerun uses the same real sealed suit recipes as the existing full-pack lunar test and records original damage sources.

chartReplyInterruptedKit.observed: The captain displayed the sealed equipment page and then resumed the star chart without pressing Back. The engineer pressed Back. A same-ship chart reply can replace the open equipment page. The fix updates the chart behind the equipment page and the regression replays the chart-opening reply while the rendered kit is visible.

profiledDedicatedAssembly.setup: Parallel survey in a loopback dedicated server with two simulated survival pilots and no client process. JDK 17 Flight Recorder profile settings were enabled.
profiledDedicatedAssembly.observation: Native assembly samples included block storage, height maps, lighting and neighbour notifications, plus chunk access and original block-entity loads. Sampling identifies the active paths but does not assign exact wall-clock time to each one.

hostedArchivedDualLanding.fixture: Two Chinese clients in survival with non-op accounts, two prepared wide ships and original sealed lunar suits.
hostedArchivedDualLanding.workflowFailure: The expected count added the furnace to the hull even though it replaces a side wall block. The corrected replay checks all 20,103 occupied blocks by count, the three actual occupied dimensions, the block entity counts, both player saves, the separate receipts and the exact head and tail cargo slots.

hostedSealedSuitAttempt.limits: The server reported success and a clean shutdown. The fixture supplied both ships and suits. The offline audit failed when the VS storage box was used as the occupied hull size, and the chunk regions were not uploaded by this run.
